newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fears for British yachtsman's safety rise.
newsitem.headline: Fears for British yachtsman's safety rise.

text.p: Fears for the safety of British round-the-world yachtsman Tony Bullimore increased on Wednesday as authorities said they believed he was now floating in the freezing Southern Ocean, away from his capsized yacht.
Australian acting Defence Minister Bronwyn Bishop said rescue officials now believed the emergency beacon attached to Bullimore, 56, was separated from the upturned hull of his yacht.
"As of today we'll be searching for that beacon which we've now established as being outside the vessel," Bishop told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

"It had been thought previously that he could have been inside the hull...but it is now thought that we should now look for that beacon because we believe of course that he could be attached to that beacon," Bishop said.
Australian airforce planes found the upturned hull of Bullimore's yacht about 1,400 miles south-west of Perth on Monday, but could not find any signs he was still alive.
Hopes that he could be alive inside the hull were raised on Tuesday when Bullimore's beacon was switched from distress mode to alarm mode, an operation that can only be done manually.

Australian Navy frigate HMAS Adelaide is currently steaming to the area from Perth and is expected to pick up another round-the-world yachtsman, Frenchman Thierry Dubois, who is huddled in a rescue dinghy next to his upturned yacht.
The two competitors in the Vendee solo round-the-world yacht race sent out distress calls from the same area late on Sunday after sailing into fierce winds and giant seas.
